headline: China says it sent forces to track USS Charleston near Sabina Shoal
deck: China said it dispatched naval forces after the U.S. ship passed Sabina Shoal; Taiwan said a Chinese coast guard cutter entered restricted waters near Pratas.
body: China’s Southern Theatre Command said it dispatched naval forces to track the USS Charleston after the U.S. littoral combat ship entered waters adjacent to Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands early Tuesday, Reuters reported. The command called the passage an illegal intrusion and said the U.S. action jeopardised maritime security. [E1][E2]

The paper’s July coverage described a Chinese maritime-authority notice of live-fire activity in two areas near Dongshan Island; Monday’s reports instead describe China’s stated action involving a U.S. ship near Sabina Shoal and a separate Taiwan Coast Guard account of contact near Pratas. [E5][E1][E3]

Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration said China Coast Guard vessel 3102 entered restricted waters northeast of Taiwan-controlled Dongsha, also known as Pratas, at about 8 a.m. It said the Taichung patrol ship monitored the cutter alongside and repeatedly ordered it away in Chinese and English; the standoff was continuing. Reuters reported that China’s Taiwan Affairs Office had no immediate comment. [E3][E4]

evidence_box.fragment: Unchecked pointer to a passage on this page beginning with the words China's military said on and ending with the words with a Chinese ship. The lead's claim (the research's own words): At 05:13 UTC / 07:13 CEST, Reuters reported that China's Southern Theatre Command said it had dispatched naval forces to track the USS Charleston after the U.S. littoral combat ship entered waters adjacent to Sabina Shoal in the Spratlys in the early hours of October 20. China characterized the passage as unauthorized and illegal; at publication time the U.S. Navy had not answered Reuters' request for comment.

evidence_box.fragment: The Chinese military’s Southern Theatre Command said the USS Charleston “illegally intruded” into waters adjacent to Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without Chinese government approval in the early hours of Tuesday. The US action infringes upon China’s sovereign rights and interests, jeopardises maritime security, and is detrimental to regional peace and stability. The US side should immediately cease such activities.
